newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao asks for protection against arrest.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao asks for protection against arrest.

text.p: Former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao asked a court on Wednesday to prevent his arrest in a criminal conspiracy case that forced him to quit as Congress party chief, local news agencies said.
Rao's lawyer asked the Delhi High Court for anticipatory bail ahead of a hearing next Monday in the $100,000 case, they said. If granted, anticipatory bail protects an accused against arrest.

On Saturday, a Delhi judge upheld a summons ordering Rao to appear in court next Monday as a co-accused in the case. Judge Ajit Bharihoke said there was sufficent evidence to suggest Rao was involved in the case.
Court officials said on Saturday that formal charges of criminal conspiracy and cheating were expected to be framed against Rao at the court hearing next week.
Rao resigned on Saturday as head of Congress, India's oldest party, shortly after the judge upheld the summons.
He had been under pressure to quit after leading Congress to its worst defeat in general elections that ended in May.
An Indian expatriate businessman, Lakhubhai Pathak, alleges Rao and a Hindu guru conspired to cheat him of $100,000 in 1983.

Pathak says he paid the money to guru Chandraswami in a failed attempt to secure a state newsprint contract after Rao, then foreign minister, assured him at a meeting in a New York hotel that his "work would be done".
Rao has said he is inocent of the allegation of criminal conspiracy to cheat, and has denied he was in New York on the dates mentioned by Pathak.
The maximum punishment Rao could face if convicted would be seven years in jail, court officials said.
The two other accused, Chandraswami and his personal assistant, are currently in judicial custody in Tihar jail, Asia's biggest prison located in the Indian capital.
Although a former prime minister and current member of parliament, Rao has no immunity in the case.
Rao's counsel argued in a petition presented to the court on Wednesday that their client was concerned he might be arrested as the two other accused were in jail, the United News of India (UNI) said.
But the petition said the case was based on circumstantial evidence and that their client should be presumed innocent, and thus not arrested, unless convicted in a trial, UNI said.

Rao was replaced on Monday as Congress chief by Sitaram Kesri, 80, a veteran party leader who swiftly reaffirmed his group's crucial support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition.
